newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes lower in nervous market.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes lower in nervous market.

text.p: The Czech PX50 fell back on Wednesday as a mood of indecison enveloped the market and dealers nervously waited for someone to take a firm lead.
The PX50 lost 5.1 points, 0.9 percent to 553.4 while the RPIX index dropped 15.2 points, 1.3 percent, to 1,152.7.
"People are definitely waiting for some kind of direction ...It's a wait and see market," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
Ivan Kusacek, a dealer at Zivnostenska Banka agreed but took a more bearish line. "I'm not very optimistic and I still don't see big interest from foreigners," he said.

Dealers said the fate of SPT Telecom, which accounts for 21 percent of index capitalisation, was still undecided as analysts continue to mull the company's 1996 results which according to international accounting standards showed a loss of 483 million crowns.
SPT recovered from heavy early losses in continuous trading on Wednesday to close down 35 crowns to 3,390.

Dealers say there are currently two evenly divided groups -- pessimists and optimists -- battling for control of the issue's direction. "At the moment they are battling...and it will take a long time," said Vystavel.
"Definitely, the figures presented yesterday were a big surprise for people but on the other hand the price (of SPT) at this level might be reasonable," added Zivnobanka's Kusacek.

With such a heavy weighting on the PX50, SPT could have a decisive influence on the market. Analysts say the current indecision surrounding the company is one of the main factors making for general uncertainty on the bourse as a whole.
Other major issues also lost ground. CEZ fell 31 crowns to 1,034, Komercni Banka dropped 38 crowns to 2,405 and IPB Banka edged one crown lower to 330.
The only highly capitalised share not to decline was savings bank Ceska Sporitelna which was unchanged at 307.
Overall on the Prague bourse, 174 shares rose, 180 fell and 110 were unchanged.
Turnover was very thin, even by recent standards, at 640 million crowns with volume at 828,189 shares.
